mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week narrowing of RETAIL_REC's negative gap over the last two weeks reflects an ongoing reopening trajectory that will continue mechanically, producing a further rise in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the same momentum persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -84.9 to -66.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior four-week improving trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp jump in PARKS mobility of more than 30 points within a single week indicates an abrupt relaxation of outdoor movement restrictions; such policy relaxation historically precedes broader reopening of retail venues within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 30 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -76.4 to -36.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks following a PARKS jump exceeding 30 points, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals households spending less time confined at home, which behaviorally translates into increased discretionary trips captured by RETAIL_REC within one week as people resume errands and leisure outings.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 31.1 to 20.6 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a continued decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates restored commuting and work-based mobility; when both rise together, the combined effect amplifies retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, because workers combine commute trips with shopping stops, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -82.1 to -65.0 and WORKPLACES rose from -66.0 to -43.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no larger than growth predicted by either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint increases in both series.

mechanism_narrative: The large simultaneous jump in PARKS alongside modest RETAIL_REC recovery suggests a seasonal shift toward outdoor and warm-weather activity that substitutes for indoor retail visits, dampening the pace of RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks even as overall mobility rises.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved far more sharply (40 points) than RETAIL_REC (14 points) over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a rate equal to or faster than PARKS over the next four weeks, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility stalls or reverses after its recent recovery (a week-on-week decline exceeding 5 points), the associated loss of commute-linked foot traffic will suppress RETAIL_REC growth within two weeks, since fewer people are passing by retail corridors during commutes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose each of the last three weeks, from -66.0 to -43.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising even after a WORKPLACES decline exceeding 5 points in a given week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery across GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and PARKS reflects a generalized behavioral unlocking of mobility (not confined to one category); the interaction of these three improving series produces compounding confidence effects that drive RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks beyond what any single series implies.
candidate_trigger: all three of GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, PARKS improve in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved concurrently from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the trend implied by any single improving series when all three move together, or declines despite joint improvement.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where restrictions were only recently eased (as evidenced by the abrupt PARKS and TRANSIT jumps between t-2w and t-1w), residual capacity limits and partial retail reopening cap how far RETAIL_REC can rise, causing growth to decelerate and plateau over the next four weeks rather than continuing at the same pace.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gain slowed from +13.6 (t-2w to t-1w) to +5.0 (t-1w to t-0w)
regime_hint: partial reopening with residual capacity restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's weekly rate of improvement accelerates rather than decelerates over the next four weeks, contradicting the plateau hypothesis.
